brief:
Tonight is Push B, and it is a deload night — the second day of the light week that runs through Sunday 27 September. Meso 3, the next hard block, starts Monday 28 September.

First, your note on the calf press last night: "Your weight suggestions make zero sense." You were right, and I went and found out why. Your recovery trainer rebuilt the card you were looking at. The number itself was honest — 190 for the calf is a fifth off the 240 you did on 13 September, exactly what a deload is meant to be. What is not honest is the sentence over it. A deload week in this app does three things at once: it takes a fifth off the weight, it cuts the number of sets to about 60%, and it drops every rep target to the bottom of its range. Only the first of those is written anywhere you can see. So the screen says "-20%" and the night in front of you is closer to half the work you did last time. On top of that, the split squat on the same card read 10 at a weight that was 57% of your last one, not 80%, because that lift is stored on two different scales in your log. You were reading a card that contradicted itself two slots above where you typed the complaint.

I can fix two of those three from here, and I have. Tonight's weights are a real fifth off what you actually logged, not a rounding-down to whatever was convenient, and the rep targets are your own working numbers rather than the bottom of the range. The set counts stay cut, because that part is the deload doing its job. What I cannot fix is the sentence on the Plan screen. It needs a code change and I am not allowed to make one.

Now the numbers. Overhead press opens the night, and on your phone it was going to open blank — that slot was swapped from the Smith press to the dumbbell press on 11 September, it has never been run on a Push B, and the app had nothing to back off from. Left alone you would have picked your own weight, and your own weight on a deload night is last month's weight. So: 35 in each hand for 10, two sets. That is a fifth off the 45s you pressed for 9 on Saturday. Chest press 130 for 10, two sets, off the 165 you did here on 14 September. Dips from the bench, two sets of 12, and stop there — you went 15, 17, 19 last time and tonight is not the night to chase that. Lateral raises: the 6 kg bells for 13, two sets. Not the 5s — 5 kg is nearly a third off the 7s you used, and that is the same over-cutting you just called out. Cable crossover 21 a side for 13, two sets; if 21 is not a notch on that stack, take the first one below it. Reverse pec deck 35 kg for 12, one set. Overhead triceps 45 for 9, two sets — you have been parked at 55 for four sessions running without ever being near failing, so 45 is the fifth off, not the 40 the app wanted. Reverse-grip pushdown 21 for 14, one set.

Every set tonight should leave you certain you had four more in you. If one feels hard, it is wrong and you should take weight off it.

One thing you should know rather than discover: you said yes to a fourth set of lateral raises yesterday. Tonight's card will show two, because the deload cuts set counts. The fourth set arrives with Meso 3 on 28 September. And while we are there — you asked on 23 August whether four sets was really right for such a small muscle group, and nobody has ever answered you. You deserve an answer before that set comes back, not after.

Two Yes/No cards are waiting, both about Meso 3 rather than tonight. Neither is urgent and both can wait until you are off the gym floor.

Off the floor: nobody has weighed you since 23 August — 207 lb, thirty days ago — and the show is 160 days out, with the prep block written in the assessment week of 2 November. A prep steers by that number and right now it is blank. Your entire log still holds one cardio session ever: 15 minutes on an elliptical, 21 July. The plan asks for two to three easy sessions a week during build blocks. Meso 3 starts in six days. This week is the cheapest week in the calendar to start both.

flags.note: Deload week, day 2 of 7 — runs through Sunday 27 September. Meso 3 starts Monday 28 September.

Your note last night was right. The Plan screen says this week is "-20%", but a deload here cuts three things at once: the weight by a fifth, the set count to about 60%, and every rep target down to the bottom of its range. Only the first is written down. The night is closer to half the work, not a fifth less. Fixing that sentence needs a code change I am not allowed to make.

Tonight's weights are a true fifth off what you actually logged, and the rep targets are your own working numbers, not the bottom of the range. Left alone the app would have prescribed 25-35% cuts under a 20% label — 10 lb lateral raises off your 7 kg, and 40 on a triceps extension you have held at 55 for four sessions.

The overhead press slot would have opened tonight with no weight at all. It was swapped from the Smith press to the dumbbell press on 11 September, has never been run on a Push B, and the deload has no cross-day carry to fall back on. I set it: 35s for 10, two sets, off the 45x9 you pressed on Saturday.
You accepted a fourth set of lateral raises yesterday. Tonight's card shows two, because the deload cuts set counts. The fourth set arrives with Meso 3 on 28 September.

Your 23 August question — "four sets seems like a lot for such a small muscle group, are you sure?" — has never been answered by anyone, and the lateral raise slot still says four. It is masked tonight and returns on 28 September.

Tonight is your fourth training day in a row and the eighth session in ten days, and six of tonight's eight lifts were trained at full Meso 2 load three days ago. No trainer vetoed on that — the deload is already the brake — but it is why nothing tonight should feel like work.

Your recovery trainer read all 32 notes in your log by hand and found no pain, tweak, pinch, strain, numbness or soreness anywhere. It reads them by hand because the automatic pain search is still broken: its only hit ever is your 23 August lateral-raise question, matched because "number" contains "numb".

The 11 September swap took the Smith overhead press off Push B because this gym has no Smith machine. The log that arrived afterwards shows you did that slot with a barbell, 115 for 7. So the heaviest overhead pressing you own has left the program, and Push B now asks for the same dumbbell press Push A already runs. Fixing it needs a barbell entry added to the exercise list — no Yes/No card can do it.

Three lifts are still named "Smith" — incline press, bent-over row and RDL — though you told the app on 2 September this gym has no Smith machine and you log them as barbell. The exercise list holds 37 entries and not one barbell entry to swap them to. Code change, not a morning review.

On last night's card the split squat read a weight that was 57% of your last one under a label promising 80%. Cause: that lift is stored on two scales in your log — 17.5 with no unit on 13 September, 7 kg on 21 September. It was a wrong number on screen and I am telling you rather than letting it pass.

No bodyweight since 23 August — 207 lb, thirty days ago, with the show 160 days out and the prep block written in the assessment week of 2 November. Prep steers by that number and it is currently blank.
Your log holds one cardio session ever: 15 minutes on an elliptical, 21 July. The plan asks for two to three easy sessions a week in build blocks. Meso 3 starts in six days.

Three trainers reported. Six disagreements, each settled by taking one side whole: the load trainer won the lateral raise, crossover, pec deck, triceps extension and pushdown; the recovery trainer won the overhead press. No vetoes, and no pain or injury objection from anyone.

proposals.why: Every set of dips you have ever logged is bodyweight, so the weight on this one can never go up — reps are the only thing that can climb. The range was raised to 12-20 reps on 14 September and that same night you finished on 19, which used up nearly all of the new room in a single session. A fourth set is the only lever left. Saying yes makes Push B a 25-set night instead of 24.

Your third set of reverse pec deck was cut last week because you had stopped doing it — two sets on 23 August, two on 2 September. That cut was decided on the morning of 14 September, a few minutes before you walked into the gym, and that night you did all three sets, twelve reps each. That is a fact the cut did not have. This asks to write the third set back before Meso 3 starts on 28 September.

overrides.reason: 35 in each hand for 10, two sets. Without this the card opens blank — this slot was swapped in on 11 September and has never been run on a Push B, so the deload had nothing to back off from. 35 is a fifth off the 45s you pressed for 9 three times on Saturday, and you have used 35s here before. Both sets should feel like four more were there.

130 for 10, two sets, off the 165 you pressed here on 14 September. Both trainers landed on this independently — it is the only lift tonight they did not argue about. Your own 10 reps stay, so the cut lands in the weight instead of in three places at once.

Two sets of 12 from the bench, and stop at 12 even though you went 15, 17, 19 on 14 September. A bodyweight lift cannot be made lighter, so the deload has to come out of the sets and the reps. This is the one place tonight where stopping early is the whole instruction.

The 6 kg bells for 13, two sets. You used 6s and 7s on 14 September, so a fifth off the 7s is 5.6 kg, which is not a dumbbell — the real choices are 5 kg and 6 kg. The app wanted 10 lb, which is 4.5 kg and is not on a kg rack at all, and would have been nearly a third off. 6 kg is the honest deload. This is exactly the shape of thing you complained about last night.

21 a side for 13, two sets, off the 27 you used on 14 September. If 21 is not a setting on that stack, take the first notch below it — I am not going to tell you what pins that machine has, because I do not know and the app no longer pretends to.

35 kg for 12, one set. Your 14 September log on this machine is explicitly 45 kg for 12, three times, and the stack moves in 5 kg steps — a fifth off 45 is 36, so 35 is the closest real setting. One set, because you already did three of these at 100 on Saturday.

45 for 9, two sets. You have been parked at 55 for four sessions running — 2, 8, 14 and 19 September — and never once been near failing, so 45 is the fifth off. The app wanted 40, which is a demotion rather than a deload on a lift you are holding cleanly.
21 for 14, one set, off the 27 you did for 13 and 15 on 14 September. Same stack as the crossover, same call. One set is what the deload leaves of a two-set lift.

dissent.progression: 35 for 9, twice — match the 9 reps he actually did at 45 on 19 September.
dissent.recovery: 35 for 10, twice — keep his own top-of-range reps so the deload lands in the weight alone.
dissent.why: Both seats independently reached 35, and both got there the same way: 45 is the only honest baseline because this slot has never been run on a Push B, and 0.8 x 45 is 36, which is not a dumbbell. So the entire argument is one rep. I took recovery's 10 because the failure this whole packet is answering is cuts stacking on top of each other without being named — weight down AND sets down AND reps down, under a label that only mentions the weight. Ten is also the top of this slot's own 8-to-10 range and is what he will do anyway at a weight this light. Progression's 9 is not wrong, it is just a third cut nobody asked for.

dissent.progression: 6 kg for 13, twice — 5 kg is a 29% cut and 6 kg is the bell he already warmed with.
dissent.recovery: 5 kg for 15, twice — 5 kg is the deload step below his 7s.
dissent.why: Both seats agree on the thing that matters and that the app got wrong: this is a kg rack, the app's 10 lb is 4.5 kg, and no such dumbbell exists — the card would have printed a weight he cannot pick up. They split on which real bell. A fifth off 7 kg is 5.6, so neither 5 nor 6 is exact, and I took the one that errs toward the label the app is showing him: 6 kg is 1 kg light of his working weight, 5 kg is nearly a third off. Last night he wrote that the suggestions made no sense, and the specific thing that made no sense was numbers cut far harder than the week claims to cut them. Choosing 5 kg here would repeat that on the very card where I am telling him I fixed it. Recovery's own reasoning names the same fault and then lands on the number that commits it.

dissent.progression: 21 a side for 13, twice — a true fifth off the 27 he used on 14 September.
dissent.recovery: 20 a side for 15, twice — leave the app's 20 alone and put the reps back to 15.
dissent.why: One pound and two reps apart, and recovery's case for 20 is that the app already chose it, which is not evidence — it is the same rounding-down that produced last night's complaint. 0.8 x 27 is 21.6, so 21 is the first real notch at or below it and 20 is a 26% cut. I agree with recovery that his working reps should survive, and 13 is inside the 12-to-15 range he lives in on this fly, so nothing is lost there. I have also told him in plain words to take the notch below 21 if 21 is not on that stack, because neither trainer can see that machine and neither should pretend to.

dissent.progression: 77.162 lb for 12, one set — that is exactly 35 kg.
dissent.recovery: 77 lb for 12, one set — described in its own note as 35 kg.
dissent.why: The two seats want the identical machine setting and wrote it down differently. Recovery says 35 kg in its reasoning and then writes 77, which is 34.93 kg and would render as 34.93 on a kg-labelled machine — an unpickable number, which is the exact fault this packet exists to stop. Progression's 77.162 is 35 kg to the gram. This is a sixth of a pound of difference and it still gets declared, because an undeclared disagreement is how things get buried here.

dissent.progression: 45 for 9, twice — 0.8 x 55 is 44, and 40 is a 27% cut on a lift he is holding cleanly.
dissent.recovery: 40 for 12, twice — leave the app's 40 and put the reps back to 12.
dissent.why: Recovery's instinct is right and its number is wrong. Its own sentence is that 40 for 8 after a month of 55 for 12 is not a set — and its answer is to keep the 40 and add reps, which is the app's over-cut with a patch on it. He has been at 55 for four consecutive sessions, on 2, 8, 14 and 19 September, hitting 12, 11, 10 and 12 reps without ever failing. A fifth off that is 44, and 45 is the step that exists. Recovery's 12 reps are also above this slot's own 8-to-10 range, so its prescription breaks the shape of the slot to compensate for a weight it did not want in the first place.

dissent.progression: 21 for 14, one set — a true fifth off the 27 he did for 13 and 15 on 14 September.
dissent.recovery: 20 for 15, one set — the app's 20, with his own 15 reps back.
dissent.why: Same argument as the crossover and settled the same way, because both seats say these two lifts read off the same stack. 0.8 x 27 is 21.6; 21 is the notch at or below it, 20 is a 26% cut. Both seats agree on one set and both agree the reps belong in the 13-to-15 band he actually works in, so the only live question was the weight, and on the weight recovery is defending a number the app rounded down rather than one it argued for.
